notes: Play knowledge rewritten as executable actions. Every reference is checked against the generated level data by tools/gen_level_nuance.py.

Archives opens with the game's clearest anti-instinct moment: the player starts beside a weapon, and taking it is the wrong move. It is a useful level for testing whether a bot can follow situational rules that contradict its defaults.

nuance.claim: The opening room holds a weapon on a table, but picking it up alerts the interrogators; the room is cleared unarmed and the weapon collected afterwards.
The two interrogators are taken down by melee rather than gunfire, which is the only fight in the game that opens this way.
After the first interrogator drops the second opens fire, and crouching makes his shots miss while closing on him.
The door key, the pistol and its ammunition are all in the opening room, so leaving early means going the rest of the level short of all three.
Natalya's room only needs its door opened; she comes out and follows, and walking in is unnecessary.
Natalya starts following the moment her door opens and is killed by crossfire, so the surrounding rooms are cleared before she is released.
The safe key is handed over by Mishkin after his dialogue rather than found or looted, so the black box objective is gated behind a conversation.
Mishkin is a uniformed officer who reads as hostile but is the source of the safe key, so shooting him removes the route to an objective.
Escaping with Natalya ends the level, so the black box must be recovered first.
nuance.because: Objective 3 is the level exit; unfinished objectives score as failed.

nuance.claim: The exit is a library window that has to be shot out and jumped through, not a door, so a bot looking for a door will never find the way out.
